items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: He played with all of us.

ctx.x: Oh, that fellow, that fellow was a famous musician. Was he from a musical family, or? He from, he from, he didn't have much, much kin, folks there, but he was a great, great, great saxophone and clarinet. Uh, yeah, but I'm trying to think of what he did, no. Could he read much, or? Could he? Ha! Sight reader. A man could read. If he hear a number playin, and he had a shirt with a cuff on it, he, he, he, he'd ride it all right, right on his cuff. Was he as good as Bichet, or T.O., or any of those people? Well,…
Did you know Charlie? He played with all of us. Hmm? He played with all of us. Yeah. Uh huh. What about Charlie Galloway? Did you know him? Charlie Galloway, I worked with, uh,

I played guitar with Charlie Galloway for a while, not too long. I believe I played with his band about two, three years. That's about all. Charlie Galloway was a bass player and he was the leader of the band. He had one leg, walked with a crutch. And he had a good Dixieland band, jazz band. And I played, I remember playing with him a while, you know. Was he an older man than you or younger? Oh yeah, he was, uh, he was younger than me. Yeah. Who was in his band? Well, uh, they had, uh, some of the old fellas out…
